blocks.text: Condo buildings in Port Guichon
River West — 4753 River Road West (also addressed 4743 W River Rd in listings), Ladner

The only named condo building confirmed inside Port Guichon. Freehold strata, plan NWS3341, managed by the Wynford Group (building directory, secondary source). The directory records 85 homes, wood-frame construction, underground/under-building garage parking, built 1991; MLS listings for units in the building record year built 1990 — the exact build year is UNCONFIRMED between those two sources.
Streets, schools and getting around Port Guichon

items.t: Port Guichon is the historic harbour pocket of west Ladner, in the City of Delta — Ladner is one of Delta's three communities (Ladner, Tsawwassen and North Delta), and Ladner and Tsawwassen together are called South Delta.

The working centre is River Road West at 46A Street: Port Guichon Elementary is at 4381 46A Street, and Ladner Harbour Park is at 4905 McNeelys Way on this shore. Official City boundary lines for the sub-area name are UNVERIFIED.

The name is historic, not a marketing label: the Canadian Register of Historic Places entry for the Victoria Terminal Railway and Ferry Company Station places the station in the historic Port Guichon neighbourhood, and the elementary school site records the school was built as Fairview Elementary and later renamed for the Guichon family.

Transit is a loop bus, not a corridor: TransLink's Ladner Exchange bay map (exchange at 4645 Harvest Drive) lists route 618, the Ladner South loop, calling at 46A Street at River Road — the Port Guichon stop; routes 601 (South Delta to Bridgeport Station), 609 and 620 also depart Ladner Exchange.

Where the condo stock concentrates: in one place only — the River Road West riverfront, where the sub-area's single named strata building stands. The rest of the confirmed stock is freehold detached housing under the RS zones and A1 Agriculture zoning toward the west edge.

Schools for the sample address 4381 46A Street, from the SD37 School Locator: Port Guichon Elementary (K–7) and Delta Secondary (8–12), 4615 51 St; catchments are address-based and other addresses are UNVERIFIED.

blocks.text: Local rules that affect condo buyers in Port Guichon

items.t: Age bylaws — only 55+ is lawful: Strata Property Act ss. 123.1 and 123.2 permit a 55+ residency bylaw; any age bylaw below 55 has been invalid since Nov 24, 2022, and the bylaw governs who may live in the unit, not who may own it. No source states River West has a 55+ bylaw — UNCONFIRMED for this building.

Flood and dike rules are the local overlay: Port Guichon is low land on the Fraser River side of Ladner behind the City's dike system; Delta operates and maintains over 63 km of flood protection infrastructure, 31 drainage pump stations and approximately 538 km of drainage infrastructure, and directs owners to DeltaMap for parcel-level flood information.

Flood covenants on title: in Ladner approvals on Chisholm Street, the City required Section 219 flood-proofing covenants and statutory rights-of-way so the dike can be raised to 5.5 metres — the pattern a buyer on river-side lots here should search title for.
Streamside rules: all properties in Delta within 30 m of a stream, including sloughs and ditches, fall within the Streamside Protection and Enhancement Development Permit Area.

Delta zoning and plan: zoning is parcel by parcel under Delta Zoning Bylaw No. 7600 (RS1, RS5, RS6 and RS7 confirmed in west Ladner; A1 Agriculture toward the west edge, with an 8-hectare minimum lot area for parcels created by subdivision). The current OCP is the consolidated Bylaw No. 8400 (2024) — no lettered schedules, no Ladner or Tsawwassen area-plan schedule; farm land is designated "Agriculture (A)."

BC Property Transfer Tax exemptions: first-time buyers — PTT exempt on the first $500,000 where fair market value is $835,000 or less (effective Apr 1, 2024), partial exemption $835,000–$860,000, land 0.5 hectares or smaller, principal residence only.

Newly built home exemption: full exemption threshold $1,100,000, phasing out to complete elimination at $1,150,000 (effective Apr 1, 2024); a never-occupied unit in a newly built condo building can qualify — relevant to new product, not to a 1990/91 resale at River West.

GST — new construction only: the FTHB GST/HST rebate (Bill C-4, royal assent Mar 13, 2026) with the new housing rebate returns 100% of GST to $1 million value, phasing to $1.5 million, maximum $50,000, agreements in the Mar 20, 2025–2031 window; the new housing rebate alone is 36% of GST, maximum $6,300, phasing out $350,000–$450,000.

blocks.text: Good to know about Port Guichon

items.t: The village next door is mid-revitalization, and it is City-led: Delta's Ladner Village Revitalization Action Plan names the Chisholm Street Wharf project in Ladner Village — the amenity story for a River West buyer is the village core, not a mall.

The dike is planned to go higher, and the paperwork can already be on title: Ladner approvals have required rights-of-way so the dike can be raised to 5.5 metres — a buyer who skips the title search misses the one local fact most likely to affect a river-side lot's future use.

This was a ferry landing before it was a neighbourhood: the Victoria Terminal Railway and Ferry Company Station stands in the historic Port Guichon neighbourhood on the Canadian Register of Historic Places, and the school on 46A Street began as Fairview Elementary before being renamed for the Guichon family.
A grocery store inside Port Guichon itself: UNVERIFIED — no source names one; the shopping is Ladner Village and the Ladner Exchange area to the east.

SSMUH quietly changed the side streets: since the June 24, 2024 adoption of Bylaws 8394 and 8395, single-detached and duplex lots here can add secondary suites, coach houses and garden suites without rezoning — the infill a River West buyer will see appearing around the older detached stock.
Recreation is the Ladner Leisure Centre, 4600 Clarence Taylor Crescent, the main Ladner recreation facility on the City's pages — not a South Delta (Tsawwassen) facility.

blocks.text: Local rules that affect townhome buyers in Port Guichon

items.t: : Port Guichon is low land on the Fraser River side of Ladner behind the City's dike system; Delta operates and maintains over 63 km of flood protection infrastructure, 31 drainage pump stations and approximately 538 km of drainage infrastructure, and directs owners to DeltaMap for parcel-level flood information.

: In Ladner approvals on Chisholm Street, the City required Section 219 flood-proofing covenants and statutory rights-of-way so the dike can be raised to 5.5 metres — the pattern a buyer on river-side lots here should search title for, on a house purchase exactly as on a strata one.

: All properties in Delta within 30 m of a stream, including sloughs and ditches, fall within the Streamside Protection and Enhancement Development Permit Area — a live constraint on adding a suite, coach house or any ground-oriented unit on a Port Guichon lot.

SSMUH / suites as Delta states them — the only route to ground-oriented added units here: Delta adopted its SSMUH zoning amendments as Bylaws 8394 and 8395 on June 24, 2024, allowing up to four units on all single-detached and duplex lots, with City support for coach houses, garden suites and secondary suites; the live feed already shows coach-house half duplexes on Savoy Street (listing copy, feed evidence only). SSMUH product is fee-simple in form unless separately strata-registered — do not market it as a townhouse complex.

Strata rules (for River West, and for townhouses east in Ladner): Form B (Strata Property Act s. 59): discloses monthly strata fees, amounts owing, approved special levies still to be paid, the CRF balance and an insurance summary, with the rules, current budget and most recent depreciation report attached; the strata must provide it within 7 days of request. Since July 1, 2024 a strata with five or more lots must obtain a depreciation report every five years and cannot vote to defer it (a sub-5-lot strata sits UNDER that threshold); since November 1, 2023 the CRF must receive a minimum of 10% of the annual operating fund each year.

blocks.text: Streets, schools and getting around Port Guichon

items.t: Municipality and plan: Ladner, one of the City of Delta's communities in South Delta, under the Delta Official Community Plan 2024, "Housing Our Future", Bylaw No. 8400, adopted July 8, 2024 — a single consolidated plan whose land-use designations sit in its Land Use Plan (s. 1.5); there is no Ladner area-plan schedule in Bylaw 8400.

The name on the ground: Port Guichon Elementary, 4381 46a St, Delta, is the BC Ministry of Education school physically in the sub-area. Nearby areas named on the page: Ladner homes generally, and Neilsen Grove — spelling lock applied throughout: the AREA is "Neilsen Grove"; the SCHOOL is "Neilson Grove Elementary".

Market position stated once, here: Port Guichon is in South Delta, and SnapStats publishes no South Delta figures — its Delta coverage is North Delta only, never used here. No Port Guichon or Ladner inventory, solds, median or days-on-market figure can be stated.

blocks.text: Local rules that affect land buyers in Port Guichon

items.t: OCP: Delta Official Community Plan 2024, Bylaw No. 8400, "Housing Our Future" — adopted July 8, 2024, a single consolidated plan with NO lettered schedules: Its Land Use Plan (s. 1.5) carries the designations, and farm land is designated "Agriculture (A)". "Schedule D.1 of Bylaw 8400" is an ERROR wherever met — the Tsawwassen Area Plan was Schedule D.1 under the previous OCP, Bylaw No. 3950.

Housing context: the City reports 1,146 net new units achieved city-wide between October 1, 2023 and September 30, 2025 against the provincial Housing Target Order — city-wide context only, not a Port Guichon figure.

ALR block (west-edge parcels where ALR status is confirmed for the parcel): ALR residences cannot be stratified (ALC Information Bulletin 09, s. 6; Strata Property Act, s. 239; Agricultural Land Commission Act, s. 21(1)); subdivision within the ALR requires ALC approval. Residence caps: principal residence ≤500 m²; a secondary suite only inside the principal residence; one additional residence of 90 m² or less on parcels of 40 ha or less, 186 m² or less on parcels over 40 ha. Farm-class thresholds in the full three-tier form: $2,500 at 0.8–4 ha; $2,500 plus 5% of the actual value of the area over 4 ha; $10,000 under 0.8 ha — applications by October 31; a flat "$2,500+" line is an ERROR.

Bare-land strata block — stated for completeness, governing no Port Guichon stock verified here: where a bare-land strata lot does exist in BC, it is strata tenure — Form B (SPA s. 59) within 7 days, max $35 plus up to 25¢/page; depreciation reports every five years for stratas with five or more lots since July 1, 2024; minimum 10% CRF contribution since November 1, 2023; rental-restriction bylaws VOID since November 24, 2022; only 55+ age bylaws valid (SPA ss. 123.1/123.2, May 1, 2023 exemptions); a "45+" listing line is NOT a valid age bylaw.

blocks.text: Good to know about Port Guichon

items.t: The geography error is the first diligence item.

One small sub-area holds two different land systems. The urban RS streets in the east and A1 Agriculture ground toward the west edge sit inside the same "Port Guichon land" search — on the land home's documented minimums, a few blocks separate a lot that subdivides at a few hundred square metres from ground that subdivides at 8 hectares. Pricing either with the other's rule set prices it wrong.

The feed's most unusual land is the river's, not the streets'. W River Road float homes, waterfront land, docks and a foreshore lease all appear in one 16-listing feed alongside ordinary house lots — the only Ladner feed in this set where foreshore tenure is part of the land picture, and the part listing copy is least able to prove.

faq.q: Which elementary school serves Port Guichon?
faq.a: Port Guichon Elementary, at 4381 46A St. — the SD37 School Locator result for that sample address is Port Guichon Elementary for K–7 and Delta Secondary for 8–12; the school was built as Fairview Elementary and renamed for the Guichon family.

faq.q: Which bus serves 46A Street at River Road?
faq.a: TransLink route 618, the Ladner South loop, calls at 46A Street at River Road, per TransLink's Ladner Exchange bay map.

faq.q: Is Port Guichon behind a dike?
faq.a: Yes — it is low river-side land protected by the City of Delta's flood protection system (dikes, seawalls and foreshore protection; over 63 kilometres of infrastructure, 31 drainage pump stations), and the City directs owners to DeltaMap for parcel-level flood information.

faq.q: Can flood covenants sit on title here?
faq.a: In Ladner approvals on Chisholm Street, the City required Section 219 flood-proofing covenants and statutory rights-of-way allowing future dike raising to 5.5 metres — buyers should search title and confirm requirements for the specific lot.
No — it is in Ladner, in west Ladner around River Road West and 46A Street; Ladner and Tsawwassen are separate Delta communities that together make up South Delta.

faq.q: How many condo buildings are there here?
faq.a: One verified: River West, 4753 River Road West, strata plan NWS3341, 85 homes per the building directory (secondary source). No townhouse complex inside the sub-area was confirmed on an official source.

faq.q: What work has River West already had done?
faq.a: A listing for a unit states a building enclosure rehabilitation was completed in 1999, with a clubhouse, fitness room, hot tub, workshop and secure parking. Treat it as listing-stated and trace the enclosure and the next capital items through the strata's depreciation report.

faq.q: Can I rent out a River West unit?
faq.a: Provincially, yes — strata rental-restriction bylaws have been void since Nov 24, 2022, and no amendment is needed for that to apply; a strata can still restrict short-term rentals. The building's own current bylaws should still be read on the Form B package.

faq.q: Are pets or ages restricted at River West?
faq.a: UNCONFIRMED — no public source read states a current pet or age bylaw for this strata. A listing's "adult-oriented setting" wording is not a bylaw; the registered bylaws attached to the strata documents are the deciding source.
No — it is in Ladner, in west Ladner around River Road West and 46A Street; Ladner and Tsawwassen are separate Delta communities that together make up South Delta.

faq.q: Are there any townhomes in Port Guichon at all?
faq.a: None verified — zero strata and zero fee-simple townhouse complexes, in the guide run and again in the batch-8 run. The stock is freehold detached housing, half duplexes, float homes and one apartment building (River West).

faq.q: Can I add a suite or coach house to a Port Guichon house instead of finding a townhouse?
faq.a: Possibly: Delta's SSMUH amendments (Bylaws 8394 and 8395, June 24, 2024) allow up to four units on single-detached and duplex lots where the zoning applies, and the feed already shows coach-house half duplexes on Savoy Street — but confirm the parcel's zone and any streamside/flood permit areas with the City first.
